treatment.approach: Grounded romantic social drama, not thriller suspense: visible reciprocal attention gives way to a restrained facial change. Natural rain-softened daylight and controlled contrast preserve the ordinary Colombo setting. Use a readable opening two-shot, clean alternating faces, the necessary caller-display detail, then listening coverage. No added street performers or business activity. The scripted material already exceeds 45 seconds; preserve every line and event rather than accelerating performance.

treatment.geography: Anudi stands frame left facing right; Kasun stands frame right facing left, with his food three-wheeler behind and to his right. All coverage stays on the road side of their axis. Anudi's left hand holds an already open umbrella with her handbag on her left forearm; her right hand receives and retains the smartphone. Kasun initially offers it in his right hand. At the end she leaves toward deep left and he returns toward deep right.
treatment.key_image: The phone that brings them together remains in Anudi's right hand as its call separates their attention.
advice: Record L11 once as a continuous eight-second phone performance; lay it across the two listening pictures, never trim or repeat it.
The 80-second bin includes handles, the indivisible take durations and essential action coverage; remove handles in the assembly, not words.

editor_notes: The must bin has 16 clips totalling 80 seconds of raw takes, under the 81-second cap. The 53-second script and minimum take sizes make the raw bin longer than the 54-second target; trim handles and overlap audio in the assembly, never compress or omit dialogue.
Use c01 for the return and L1, c02 for L2 and the look toward the business, the B/C singles for the exchange, and c07 for admiration. Keep the screen direction and the prop hands matched.
Use c08 to show the readable caller ID and the acceptance before the remote voice. Add the ring, rain, traffic and end tone in post where silent-source generation suppresses sound.

L11 is one uninterrupted eight-second phone performance, recorded separately in full and laid across c10 and c11: use three seconds over c10 and five seconds over c11, with their handles outside those picture intervals. The checker still reports the full line against each short picture take; do not treat either report as permission to trim, repeat or reword the line. Match Anudi's gradually fading smile across the cut.
Match the right-hand phone from c08 through the ear position in c09-c12 and the lowered position in c13. Kasun can observe Anudi's expression but does not hear the remote words.
In the handover, keep the performers' hands on separate ends of the phone and avoid visible body contact. Maintain the same open umbrella in Anudi's left hand and handbag on her left forearm.

c16 starts with Anudi already facing away; use the preceding reverse to bridge the skipped turn. She exits left before Kasun turns toward the vehicle. Do not add an invented work action or explain his thoughts.

No speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in or split screen is requested; if editorially desired, create it in post from the clean source and preserve dialogue timing. Avoid mirrors, fast finger work, contact between bodies and sharply staged crowds.

editor_notes: The must bin has 16 clips totalling 80 seconds of raw takes, under the 81-second cap. The 53-second script and minimum take sizes make the raw bin longer than the 54-second target; trim handles and overlap audio in the assembly, never compress or omit dialogue.
Use c01 for the return and L1, c02 for L2 and the look toward the business, the B/C singles for the exchange, and c07 for admiration. Keep the screen direction and the prop hands matched.
Use c08 to show the readable caller ID and the acceptance before the remote voice. Add the ring, rain, traffic and end tone in post where silent-source generation suppresses sound.

L11 is one uninterrupted eight-second phone performance, recorded separately in full and laid across c10 and c11: use three seconds over c10 and five seconds over c11, with their handles outside those picture intervals. The checker still reports the full line against each short picture take; do not treat either report as permission to trim, repeat or reword the line. Match Anudi's gradually fading smile across the cut.
Match the right-hand phone from c08 through the ear position in c09-c12 and the lowered position in c13. Kasun can observe Anudi's expression but does not hear the remote words.
In the handover, keep the performers' hands on separate ends of the phone and avoid visible body contact. Maintain the same open umbrella in Anudi's left hand and handbag on her left forearm.

c16 starts with Anudi already facing away; use the preceding reverse to bridge the skipped turn. She exits left before Kasun turns toward the vehicle. Do not add an invented work action or explain his thoughts.

No speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in or split screen is requested; if editorially desired, create it in post from the clean source and preserve dialogue timing. Avoid mirrors, fast finger work, contact between bodies and sharply staged crowds.
